steps.text: Combine eggs, vanilla and raisins in a small bowl; cover and let stand for 1 hour.
Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).

Beat butter, brown sugar, and white sugar together in a large bowl until creamy. Sift flour, cinnamon, and baking soda together; stir into the creamed mixture. Stir in the raisin mixture, oats, and pecans.

Drop by teaspoonfuls onto an ungreased baking sheet. Bake in the preheated oven until lightly browned, about 10 minutes. Let cool briefly on the baking sheets before transferring to wire racks to cool completely.

raw_recipe.headline: Raisin Oatmeal Pecan Cookies
raw_recipe.description: Tender and chewy oatmeal raisin cookies packed with chopped pecan nuts. The secret is in the soaking of the raisins!

review.reviewBody: Okay, after reading the previous reviews, I think I have a few pointers. Anyone who is having flat cookies is probably not letting the butter soften naturally. This is definitely important - if you use the microwave to soften the butter your cookies will certainly flatten. If you are still having flat cookies you can try and use baking powder instead of baking soda. The next suggestion is to add at least 2 tsp. cinnamon (and possibly some allspice and cloves if you like those flavors - 1/2 tsp. of each). This recipe calls for rolled oats - but this does not mean traditional cooking oats - they are rolled oats also, but so are quick 1-minute oats and they will soften in the oven whereas the traditional oats will not. And whatever reviewer suggested mixing the dough with your hands was a genius. My hands worked so much better than a spoon. And make sure to use 3 jumbo eggs or 4 large eggs to give it enough to keep it together. These cookies when prepared correctly are wonderful. By far the best oatmeal raisin cookie I have ever made!

Excellent, entire batch gone in one day! I've already given out this recipe 4 times! I made a few adjustments...half golden raisins, 1 cup walnuts, 1 tsp baking powder and 1 tsp baking soda, 2 tsp cinnamon, 1/2 tsp ground cloves. I also soaked the raisins in 2 eggs and added 1 egg to the batter for easier mixing. Soaking the raisins in the egg makes the difference, never skip this step!

I'm not a big baker but being cooped up in the house with this quarantine, I think we're all finding new hobbies! These cookies were DEE-LISH!! So I made this with only 3 minor changes to the recipe. I took the advice of a few reviewers and used an extra egg so 4 in total. I also did 1 teaspoon baking soda and 1 teaspoon baking powder. The only other add was a little salt. I'm surprised there wasn't at least a pinch included in the recipe. Maybe because there's salt in the butter? Idk. But I thought it was definitely missing when I took my first bite. Other than that, I used parchment and made sure the pans were cool (ran cold water over them and dried--takes 4 seconds) before every new batch. I also chilled the dough for just a few minutes before the first batch and then kept it in the fridge between batches--just to further help the cookies not over spread. I brought my butter to room temp the right way (for once) as I read this is more important than given credit for...and I used old fashioned oats, which I read was recommended for cookies like these. Oh, and I used a medium sized ice cream scoop so they were all relatively the same size. Great recipe! Thank you! :)

I used applesauce in place of butter because of dairy allergies, and replaced cinnamon with 1/2 tsp. allspice + 1/2 tsp. cardamom. I also split the recipe into three batches: one basic recipe (with stated alterations) and one with shredded coconut as breakfast cookies; and a snack batch with chocolate chips.

I have made these both as written and as a diabetic snack for my husband using truvia and Splenda blend brown sugar. Just remember that when measuring the brown sugar, you must use only 1/2 the amount of Splenda brown sugar so 1 cup brown sugar equals 1/2 cup of the Splenda blend. Also, when making the diabetic version, I flattened the cookies slightly before baking them as they do not spread out as well as the regular cookies. Both versions are awesome !

This is the best recipe. I used a cup of golden and a cup of regular raisins. TIP! If you’re getting flat cookies is because you’re not chilling the dough. I ALWAYS bake cookies after being in the freezer for at least 30 minutes or totally frozen. If the butter is room temp and then you bake, the butter will just melt and spread your cookie out. Give that a try and see if it works!

Very easy and super fast cookies to make. I followed the directions exactly except subbed 1 cup of white whole wheat for 1 cup of all purpose flour and added an extra 1/2 tsp. of cinnamon. I was a little worried that the cookies would be dry because the dough was on the dry side but they turned out great! Baked for 9 minutes on parchment on waffle bottom cookie sheets.

I used some of the recommendations from other reviewers plus I changed some things up to make it an Autumn cookie. I used a mix of dried cranberries, almonds and cashews instead of raisins and pecans. I added half a teaspoon pumpkin spice as well. The recommendations I used from other reviewers: I used 4 eggs instead of 3 and I replaced the baking soda with baking powder. The cookies were very fluffy compared to when I made them before. 

Previously I made this recipe with the baking soda it calls for. I didn't replace it with baking powder, but I used 4 large eggs instead of 3. I also added 1/4 teaspoon-ish of cloves. Also turned out really good. 

Thanks for sharing your awesome recipe. It's my favorite cookie now.

Solid straight forward recipe. I change it up and replicated a cookie I had at Bandon Dunes about 10 years ago. Keep entire recipe the same just take the 1 cup or raisins and bring that to 1/4 cup. Add 1/4 cup dried cranberries, 1/4 cup semi sweet chocolate chips, 1/4 cup white chocolate chips + 1/2 cup shredded coconut and decrease oats to one cup. This then becomes an award winning cookie with a unique taste.

Thank you for the great recipe! I used baking powder instead of using baking soda to make them fluffier/softer and I added nutmeg and ground cloves. I make them for my grandparents sometimes and they love them!

Delicious if I say so myself. I made a few modifications/additions. Modifications: 1 minute quick oats, 1/2 tsp vanilla extract (I ran out) Used Baking powder instead of soda Added 1tsp of cloves Added 1tsp of all spice Be sure to let the butter sit at room temp for 1 hour while the raisin, egg, vanilla sit I ground glazed pecans instead of using the whole/chopped nut. I think the glazed pecan made up the missing vanilla.
I made my jumbo, so I only came out with 2 dozen. So I had to bake them 3 minutes longer.
Had a hard time getting them to bake evenly. Liked the way the raisins softened up.
when doing gluten free cook for about 4x longer
Fantastic. Best oatmeal raisin recipe ever. I followed it exactly. Made so many cookies. Be prepared to eat or freeze!!!
